blocks.text: What an AI assistant for Word on Mac does

Word is a large app with many hidden corners. Most people use the same handful of features every week. The rest of the ribbon is a search problem. An AI assistant for Word on Mac helps with that search. Lazur lives in the notch at the top of your screen. You hold a key, speak, and it answers out loud. It looks at what is on screen, points at controls, and guides you through steps. It also drafts text at your cursor and takes dictation.
Six things you can ask Lazur in Word

items: Explain what is on screen, such as a change bar, a warning, or a menu you do not know.
Point at a control. Lazur circles the button and labels it on your screen.
Guide you through a feature. Lazur gives one step, then waits for your click.
Draft text at the cursor, such as a summary or a first paragraph.
Dictate text at the cursor with the fn key held down.
Handle everyday tasks while you work, such as a timer or an Apple Reminders item.

blocks.text: Lazur does not operate Word for you. It does not click buttons, edit files, or run other apps. That limit shapes how you use it. When you need a result, you still make the clicks. Lazur tells you which click to make and why. Lazur is also not a plugin or add-in for Word. It runs beside Word. Think of it as a sharp helper on the side, not a second person at the keyboard.
Ask what is on screen in Word on Mac

Hold ⌥ ⌘, which is Option and Command together, then ask your question. Lazur looks at your screen only while you hold the keys. It answers out loud. Ask in plain words. You do not need the official name of a feature. Describe the spot on the page instead. Say 'the grey box above the table' or 'the red line next to the third paragraph.' Lazur can use that description to find the right place.

Word has a lot of marks that confuse people. Change bars are one example. They appear in the margin when Track Changes is on, and someone may have turned it on without telling you. A good answer from Lazur names the feature, says what the mark means, and tells you where the setting lives. In Word for Mac, Track Changes sits on the Review tab. Ask Lazur to circle it if you want to see it.

blocks.title: Keep the page in view
blocks.text: Lazur reads what is on screen at the moment you hold the keys. If you scroll to a different section, hold the keys again. An answer about the wrong section is usually a scroll problem, not a Lazur problem.
Point at a button you cannot find

The Word ribbon can look different in a smaller window. Some groups move or hide. Ask Lazur to point at the Dictate button. It circles the button and labels it. You still press it. If the button is missing, check your subscription first. Microsoft says the Dictate button may not show without a Microsoft 365 subscription.

Pointing helps in three situations. A feature moved between versions. A menu label is unfamiliar. A button is grey and you cannot tell why. Lazur can name the control. It cannot switch the control on for you. Grey buttons often need the right text selected or the right kind of object active. Select the text first, then ask again.

Ribbon labels change slowly, but they do change. The release notes for Word Version 16.114.3, dated October 27, 2026, list only quality and performance improvements. Microsoft's update history shows a newer build, 16.114.4, dated November 4, 2026. Check the label on your own screen. Ask Lazur to point at it, and trust the screen over an old tutorial.
Walk through a feature one click at a time

Guide mode fits longer jobs. Ask Lazur to walk you through a table of contents, a citation, or a template. It gives one step and waits. You click. Then Lazur moves to the next step. That pace matters in Word. Many features depend on what you selected a moment ago. A guide that stops at each click lets you catch a wrong step early.

Here is a worked example. Say 'Walk me through a table of contents.' In Word for Mac, the path starts on the References tab. Lazur points at that tab, then waits. Click it. Lazur then points at the Table of Contents group and waits again. If your section titles lack heading styles, the table comes out empty. Apply heading styles first, then build the table.

Shortcuts beat guides once a feature becomes routine. Microsoft lists the Mac shortcuts in the table below. Some of them may conflict with macOS defaults. Microsoft says you can clear those conflicts under Mission Control in Keyboard settings. It also says standard function keys can be turned on in Keyboard preferences. If F1 does not undo, check that setting first.

blocks.text: Draft text at the cursor in Word

Draft mode writes text and types it at your cursor. Use it for a first pass, not a final draft. Say 'Draft a two-sentence summary of the section above.' Lazur reads the page, writes the lines, and types them where the cursor sits. Then you read, change, and keep what works. You stay in charge of the words that leave your desk.

Drafting fails in a few known ways. The text can repeat a point from earlier. It can include a number that is not in the document. It can flatten your voice. Read every sentence before you send the file. Check each figure against a source you opened. If a firm or clinic policy covers AI use, follow that policy first.
Checks before you keep an AI draft

items: Check every number against a source you can open.
Read the first and last sentence of each paragraph for tone.
Delete any sentence that repeats an earlier point.
Save a copy before you accept a long draft.

blocks.text: Dictate text in Word on Mac, two ways

Word and Lazur both offer dictation, and they use different keys. Microsoft's dictation page says you can start Word dictation with ⌥ F1. Word dictation needs a Microsoft 365 subscription, a microphone, and a reliable internet connection. Without a subscription, the Dictate button may be missing.

On some MacBook keyboards, F1 needs the fn key held down. A 2023 Microsoft Q&A answer suggests ⌥ fn F1 for that case. The answer was not accepted, so test it yourself. If F1 changes the screen brightness, turn on standard function keys in Keyboard settings. Then try ⌥ F1 again.

blocks.text: Lazur dictation works differently. Hold fn, speak, and release. Lazur writes clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. It keeps snippets, a personal dictionary, and clipboard slots. Use snippets for text you repeat, such as an address block or a signature. Use the personal dictionary for names and terms your documents use often.

Check the current trial and plan details on the pricing page before you choose. Then test both options on one paragraph. Compare the text that lands in the document. Keep the option you trust for that kind of writing.
Real tasks people bring to Word on Mac

Microsoft does not publish a most-viewed list for Word. Its Word for Mac help page shows a sample of articles instead. The sample covers keyboard shortcuts, Track Changes, comments, templates, tables of contents, and citations. That list is the best public hint about what people look up. It is not a ranking, though.

Formatting is the loudest complaint in the research. A SquarePact blog post says it ran a survey where 96% of Word users struggled with formatting. The post names no sample size and no method. Treat that number as a vendor claim, not a measured fact. Still, it lines up with topics Microsoft covers, such as Track Changes and tables of contents.

Formatting usually breaks for a few reasons. Styles get applied in different ways. A pasted block carries old fonts with it. Track Changes is on when you did not expect it. Lazur can explain each one as it appears on screen. Ask 'Why did this paragraph change font?' Name the paragraph, and Lazur answers about that spot.
Mac and Word requirements to check first

Word on Mac needs at least 4 GB of RAM and 10 GB of free disk space. Microsoft lists a 1280 x 800 minimum display. It also asks for one of the three most recent macOS versions. Updates to Office apps need macOS 12 or later. Check your Mac version before you update, not after.

Older Macs have a harder deal. Microsoft says that from July 13, 2026, a Mac that misses the requirements can open and print Office files. It cannot edit or save them. That date has passed. If Word will not save on your Mac, check your macOS version first. Click Apple menu > About This Mac.

Lazur runs on Mac with Apple silicon or Intel. It does not run on Windows. Windows is planned, not available. Lazur needs permission to use the microphone and to see your screen. Allow both when macOS asks. Without them, Lazur cannot hear or see your question.
Big files and the 512 MB limit

Word can open files up to 512 MB, according to a Microsoft Learn limits page. That page is marked archived, so treat the number as a guide. The page also lists a 32 MB limit for total document text. It excludes graphics. A file full of images can pass 32 MB and still open.

Long files also make assistants work harder. Lazur sees what is on your display, not the whole file. Scroll to the section you need before you hold the keys. A question about a late section works better when that section is on screen.
Privacy for confidential Word documents

Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Read those facts before you open a client file, a contract, or a medical record.

Sending a screenshot to an outside provider is still a real step. Check your firm or company rules first. Close or hide anything you should not share before you hold the keys. If you work with legal files, see [Word for lawyers on Mac](/for/lawyers/word) for the Track Changes and clause review workflow.
Mistakes people make with an AI assistant in Word

items: Expecting Lazur to click. It points and guides. You click.
Holding the keys while the page shows the wrong section. Lazur sees only what is on screen.
Asking about a feature without describing the spot on the page.
Trying Word dictation without a subscription. The Dictate button may be missing.
Pressing ⌥ F1 on a MacBook without checking whether the fn key is needed.
Trusting a draft without reading each sentence.

blocks.text: One more mistake shows up often. People ask a big question in one breath. Ask about one control or one section at a time. Short questions get clear answers. Long ones tend to get vague answers, so split them up.
Set up your first Word session with Lazur

items: Install Lazur from the [download page](/download).
Open a document in Word and keep the window in view.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask what is on screen.
Hold fn and dictate one sentence into the document.
Ask Lazur to walk you through a table of contents, then stop after the first step.

blocks.text: There is a free trial with no credit card. Check the current length and plan details on the [pricing page](/pricing). Then decide whether you need Lazur for Word tasks, dictation, or both.
What to do next with Word on Mac

Pick one task you repeat each week. Ask Lazur to point or guide you through it. Write the steps down in your own words. Then learn the shortcuts for the steps you repeat most. Keep Word dictation and Lazur dictation on separate keys, so you can compare them on real work.

Check your Word version under Word > About Word before you trust a tutorial. Microsoft's update history lists build 16.114.4, dated November 4, 2026. If your version differs, ask Lazur to point at the label you see.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Word on Mac?
faq.answer: Lazur works beside Word. It is not an add-in, and it does not click for you. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about the screen. Lazur answers out loud, points at controls, and guides you through steps.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my Word document for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur drafts text and types it at your cursor when you ask. It does not edit files or click Word's buttons. You make the final changes and decide what stays in the document.

faq.question: Do I need a Microsoft 365 subscription for dictation?
faq.answer: Word's built-in Dictate needs one. Microsoft says dictation is only for Microsoft 365 subscribers and needs a microphone and a reliable internet connection. Lazur dictation is a separate feature. You hold fn to use it.

faq.question: What is the Word dictation shortcut on Mac?
faq.answer: Microsoft lists ⌥ F1. On some MacBook keyboards, you may need ⌥ fn F1. If F1 changes the screen brightness, turn on standard function keys in Keyboard settings and try again.

faq.question: Which Macs can run Word for Mac?
faq.answer: Microsoft's system requirements list 4 GB of RAM, 10 GB of free disk space, a 1280 x 800 minimum display, and one of the three most recent macOS versions. Updates to Office apps need macOS 12 or later. Older Macs may open and print files but cannot edit or save them.

faq.question: How big a Word file can Word open?
faq.answer: Microsoft's archived Learn page lists 512 MB as the file size Word can open. The same page lists a 32 MB limit for total document text, and it excludes graphics. Treat both numbers as guides, since the page is marked archived.

faq.question: Is my document sent to AI providers?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to get an answer. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Hide anything you should not share before you hold the keys.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Word on Windows?
faq.answer: No. Lazur runs on the Mac, with Apple silicon or Intel. Windows is planned, not available. Check the download page for the current platform list.

faq.question: Where do I find my Word version on Mac?
faq.answer: Open Word > About Word. Microsoft's update history lists build 16.114.4, dated November 4, 2026, as the newest Word for Mac update in the history it publishes.
